title: Lease fencing: only the current generation commits; a late stale worker is rejected and its log kept
note: Synthetic. Lists the function exercised, the input and the expected outcome; authored, not run. No number here is a measurement of real rendering, latency, memory or cost.

calls.case: same node, input digest and approval twice
worker A claims (generation 1); worker B claims while A's process is alive
an upstream revision lands while A runs; B claims (generation 3)
A wakes up and commits its staged output with generation 1
B commits with generation 3 but current_input_digest differs from the job's
B commits with the right generation and digest
agent job accepted by crew.mjs check with a stale token
a lease whose owner pid is dead; and one whose pid was reused by another process

expect: the second create returns created false and the same job (idempotent by node + input + approval)
B's claim is refused lease_held while A's owner identity is alive, however old A's heartbeat is
supersede bumps the generation and returns stop_pid for the live local owner; B's claim becomes generation 3
A's commit is rejected stale_generation; its staged directory is moved to crew/jobs/rejected/ and attempts/<job>-a1.log records the rejection; nothing is published
an upstream input change rejects the commit with input_changed and keeps the staged output
a valid commit renames the staged files into the run atomically and records the output manifest (path, digest, size); the lock was held only for checks and renames
accept with a stale token is refused and logged; crew.mjs check turns it into a problem and does not record ok
a dead owner (or a changed pid start time) allows the claim and logs the reclaim; a live owner never does
